votes.reason: Confirmed at abbf066 by inspection, no experiment required. R72 (08-contracts-v1-encoding.md §10, line 230) rules "a NONZERO legacy USD balance is a rollout hold" and 04-verification.md CREDIT-UNITS names "nonzero/negative USD histories". The shipped predicate in apps/app/supabase/migrations/0015_signup_eligibility.sql:120 (`coalesce(sum(delta_usd),0) <> 0`) is correct. But every public.claim_signup_grant call in the suite reaches a personal org whose legacy sum is 0 or +5: check_eligibility (checks_signup.py:177-190) seeds h=+5 and z=+5/-5=0; SHARED holds via the shared-org predicate, not USD; the backfill check asserts all HOSTED users have USD 0.00000000; check_signup_privileges claims an unconfirmed user with no USD; the scenario's negative sums (checks.py:119-127, org_a/org_b with -3, -12.345678) belong to legacy orgs no signup claim targets. So the `<> 0` -> `> 0` mutant necessarily survives (h still holds, z still grants). The only other `<> 0` hold predicate (0008 console_legacy_usd_statement) is inlined, does not call infrx.legacy_usd_rollout_hold, and its checks_credit test uses ORG_A with a positive sum anyway. The registered mutant a1_usd_balance_not_a_hold (signup_mutants.py:46-49, `and false`) only defends the positive half. The negative case is not speculative: checks.py:120-123 documents that the deployed console writes negative grants today and production may hold them. Blocking under the stated rule (invariant with no killable test); fix is one negative-balance individual in check_eligibility plus optionally registering the `> 0` mutant.

Confirmed at abbf066 by code inspection. `infrx.legacy_usd_rollout_hold` (apps/app/supabase/migrations/0015_signup_eligibility.sql:118-121) is correct (`coalesce(sum(delta_usd),0) <> 0`), and R72 (08-contracts-v1-encoding.md:230) / CREDIT-UNITS (04-verification.md:38, "nonzero/negative USD histories") require negative balances to hold. But the only legacy-USD seeds anywhere in the signup suite are checks_signup.py:179-181: h = +5 (asserted rollout_hold), z = +5/-5 = 0 (asserted granted). Under the mutant `<> 0` -> `> 0`: h 5>0 true (hold, passes), z 0>0 false (granted, passes); the `shared` individual (checks_credit.SHARED, personal org with no USD rows) reaches rollout_hold via 0006's 55000 exception on either branch, with the identity claim rolled back, so its assertions also pass. No other check (binding, privileges, race, retirement, backfill, test_signup.py) inserts delta_usd rows, and the credit scenario's negative-balance ORG_B is not any claimant's personal org. The 0008 console statement's own inline `<> 0` (checks_credit.py:1375-1383, ORG_A net positive) is a separate function and does not exercise 0015's. The shipped mutant `a1_usd_balance_not_a_hold` (signup_mutants.py:46-49) only kills the `and false` variant. So the negative half of R72's "nonzero" invariant has no killable test: the reviewer's surviving mutant is reproducible from the code alone. Not a runtime defect; a coverage gap on a money/eligibility invariant, which the review rubric classes as blocking. Fix is minimal: one individual with a single negative legacy row (e.g. usage -0.000001) asserting rollout_hold and wallet_of is None, plus the `<> 0` -> `> 0` mutant in MIGRATION_MUTANTS.

No test exercises a post-retirement operator_adjustment, inference_debit or hold settle/release, so the acceptance half of the frozen-wallet contract is unkillable.

confirmed_blocking.minimal_fix: In check_retirement, after retire(t): assert attempt(insert operator_adjustment into wt) is None and assert attempt(insert inference_debit for the pre-retirement hold + update hold state='settled') is None (about 6 lines, using checks_credit.attempt). votes.reason: Confirmed at abbf066 from the code alone. The acceptance half of the frozen-wallet contract is stated four times as A1's invariant: migration comment (apps/app/supabase/migrations/0015_signup_eligibility.sql:86-88), evidence table item 5 and integration request 7 (research/plan/evidence/a/A1-38aea7f.md:34, :199), and proposed ruling R-A1 (:149 "In-flight settlement and D5 compensating entries still land"). The shipped triggers do encode it (ledger guard is `when (new.kind = 'signup_grant')`, holds guard is `before insert` only), but nothing tests it. check_retirement (apps/infrx-api/tests/d/checks_signup.py:399-470) after retire(t) does: a second retire, profile/keys/suspension reads, `refused(... spend ...)` (a NEW hold, refused either way), a control hold on another wallet, claim(t) (answers `retired`, no ledger write), a money read, grant-seam refusal into n's wallet (signup_grant kind, refused either way), a hard-delete refusal, and identity reuse. The pre-retirement `spend` ran through `attempt`, which rolls back, so wt has no hold rows to update. retire_individual itself writes only retired_individuals, profiles and api_keys (0015 lines 230-236), no ledger or hold rows. So a mutant dropping the `when` clause or adding `or update` to the holds trigger changes no observable in check_retirement, and the migration-mutant runner executes only the named check (migration_mutants.py:1276/1306), so both reviewer mutants survive without needing a run. No other tests/d or state module exercises post-retirement settlement (grep). R32 requires every named invariant to be killable; R40 makes a surviving money mutant block the owning track's integration; this one gates D5's settlement/adjustment behaviour for retired wallets, i.e. money. The proposed fix (two `attempt(...) is None` asserts after retire(t) using a real, committed pre-retirement hold, plus two list entries) is the right minimal shape.

Confirmed from code at abbf066. 0015 lines 96-107 freeze only hold INSERTs and signup_grant ledger INSERTs; nothing else references retired_individuals, so the shipped behaviour (operator_adjustment, inference_debit and hold settle/release still accepted after retirement) matches the migration comment and integration request 7. But checks_signup.check_retirement's only pre-retirement hold goes through checks_credit.attempt, which rolls back, and after retire(t) the check performs only refusals, a SELECT and a claim that answers 'retired' before any ledger write. It never inserts a non-grant ledger row into the retired wallet nor updates a hold on it, so rv_ledger_freeze_all_kinds (drop the `when (new.kind = 'signup_grant')` clause, unique anchor) and rv_holds_freeze_on_update (`before insert` -> `before insert or update`, unique anchor) survive by construction; signup_mutants.MIGRATION_MUTANTS only cover the refusal half. The acceptance half is a stated money invariant handed to D5/D2 (evidence item 5, IR 7); R32 requires every named invariant to be killable and R40 names money survivors as blocking. The ~6-line fix (commit a hold before retire, then assert attempt(operator_adjustment) is None and attempt(inference_debit + hold state='settled') is None; add the two mutants) kills both.

MEASURED on a scratch copy of abbf066 (port 55714, container infrx-review-a1-verify-2-0-postgres, removed afterwards; probe /tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/apps/infrx-api/tests/d/review_probe_verify.py, run against the plain image via the D harness with seed_fixtures + seed_credit, one granted individual retired via infrx.retire_individual, then statements issued under checks._jwt(<retired user>)):

- P5 `update public.api_keys set revoked_at = null where created_by = <retired>` -> REFUSED 23514 "audience and scope are immutable; revocation is one-way". The reviewer missed 0009_operator_seams.sql:78-101: `infrx.api_keys_identity_guard` is a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE row trigger on public.api_keys that raises when `old.revoked_at is not null and new.revoked_at is distinct from old.revoked_at`; it fires for every role, so 0001's `api_keys_update_owner` policy and 0004:152's column grant cannot un-revoke. The headline break ("revoked keys cannot authenticate afterwards") is therefore false: no revoked key can be made to authenticate again.
- P8 `update public.profiles set email = ...` -> REFUSED 42501 (0001 grants only full_name, avatar_url). The anonymised address stays anonymised.
- P6 insert of a NEW key into the suspended personal org -> ALLOWED (retired user keeps owner membership; `public.is_org_owner` still true). P7 `update profiles set full_name` -> ALLOWED.

Why P6/P7 are not blocking: the org is suspended (measured `suspended = true`, audited) and the wallet is frozen (0015:85-95 raises 23514 on any new hold; killed mutant a1_retired_wallet_spends), so a freshly minted key gets a TenantSession that is refused `org_suspended` on admission/feedback (R33, contracts/conformance/jobs.py:261-265, operations/service.py:224) and can never reserve CREDIT; it can read only its own suspended org. full_name is the user voluntarily re-entering their own display name on their own retired account; the retained PII the policy anonymises (email) cannot be restored. Both also require a live session, and the documented flow (0015 header; R-A1 proposal in research/plan/evidence/a/A1-38aea7f.md) is GoTrue soft delete first, which deletes the user's sessions/refresh tokens; the `retire-user` CLI the claim leans on does not exist at abbf066 (integration request 5 is a proposal for G6B, not code). No ruling in 08 §10 (R59, R64-R66 read) requires retire_individual to revoke the GoTrue session or strip membership. Optional hardening for the coordinator, not a gate: have retire_individual refuse unless auth.users.deleted_at is set, or add a retired_individuals check to api_keys_insert_owner/profiles_update_self, with a check_retirement case under _jwt(retired user).

The central claim (a retired user's own session sets revoked_at = null on its keys) is false at abbf066, measured, not just static. 0009_operator_seams.sql:83-101 installs `infrx.api_keys_identity_guard`, a security-definer BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on public.api_keys that raises 23514 'revocation is one-way' whenever `old.revoked_at is not null and new.revoked_at is distinct from old.revoked_at`; triggers fire regardless of role or column grant, and no migration after 0009 (0015 included) drops or disables it. It is already covered by a killable test: checks_credit.py:1838 'un-revoking a key' in the refused list, with mutant `d1r_key_unrevoked` (migration_mutants.py:1113) in test_migration_mutants' default subset. Live probe (scratch container infrx-review-a1-verify-2-1-postgres on 55715, full migration chain + seeds, then `_jwt(retired user)`): `update public.api_keys set revoked_at = null where created_by = X` -> REFUSED 23514 'audience and scope are immutable; revocation is one-way'; key still revoked. So 'revoked keys cannot authenticate afterwards' holds on the retire-only path. The two secondary sub-claims are true but not the invariant and not blocking: the same session CAN insert a new key into its suspended personal org (policy `api_keys_insert_owner`, owner row kept) and CAN rewrite full_name (`profiles_update_self`). Measured consequences: `infrx.key_by_hash` reports the new key with org_suspended = true, and a hold against that org/wallet is refused 23514 'CREDIT wallet ... is frozen: its owner is retired', so the key cannot spend; a name the user types back into their own profile is not a leak. The documented deletion request (A1 evidence 'Ruling proposal', 0015 comment) is GoTrue soft delete THEN retire_individual, and soft delete ends the session; the `retire-user` CLI is an unimplemented G6B integration request, not code at abbf066. Residual (nonblocking hardening, pre-existing 0001/0009 behaviour for any suspended org, not A1's): an owner of a suspended org can still create keys/rename; the legacy `auth/keys.py` selects only id,org_id,revoked_at and does not consult org_suspended, which is a D2/gateway concern already noted in A1 evidence item 8.

At abbf066 the mutant R3_hold_returns_amount would survive, but only because the reviewer built it to be behaviour-equivalent (3 coordinated edits: returns numeric, drop `<> 0`, add `<> 0` at the call site). R32 requires one single-edit mutant per invariant; an equivalent multi-edit mutant surviving is not a suite failure. More importantly, "returns boolean, never an amount" is not an invariant in 08-contracts-v1-encoding.md §10: R64 (unit is a type), R65 (no conversion), R72 (nonzero legacy USD balance is a rollout hold, neither converted nor discarded) and R73 (totals per unit, no combined CREDIT+USD total) are all still satisfied by a USD-only function returning a USD amount — the mutant converts nothing and combines nothing. The schema already sanctions exactly that shape: public.console_legacy_usd_statement (0008_credit_read_surface.sql:157-171) returns coalesce(sum(l.delta_usd),0) from public.credit_ledger next to a rollout_hold boolean. The evidence sentence in A1-38aea7f.md item 2 states its invariant as "no function reads both units" (R64/R73), which is measured: check_no_unit_conversion (checks_credit.py:641-670) caught the original defect of claim_signup_grant summing delta_usd inline (failure drill 2, fixed at 38aea7f), and that is the realistic single-edit regression; R72 itself is killed by a1_usd_balance_not_a_hold (signup_mutants.py:46). The proposed pg_get_function_result = 'boolean' check would test code shape rather than any ruling, and the "no numeric-returning function reads delta_usd outside the USD read surface" rule does not exist in §10.

The reviewer's static fact is correct but the conclusion (blocking) does not follow. Confirmed at abbf066 by reading and by running the scan's tokeniser on a string copy with the 3 edits applied: `checks_credit.check_no_unit_conversion` (checks_credit.py:641-670) is a name-token scan; the mutated `legacy_usd_rollout_hold` tokenises as USD-only (`delta_usd`, `public.credit_ledger`) and `claim_signup_grant` as CREDIT-only (`signup_entitlements`), no check in tests/d reads `prorettype`/`pg_get_function_result`, and the function is not in `credit_schema.SEAMS`, so mutant R3_hold_returns_amount would survive. However: (1) it is behaviour-equivalent (the reviewer concedes 'behaviour is identical'), so it is not a real defect — every caller path answers the same `rollout_hold`; (2) it is a 3-edit mutant, outside R32's 'one single-edit mutant per invariant' standard; (3) the invariant it targets ('returns boolean, never an amount') is not one any ruling binds: R73 forbids combined cross-unit totals (a USD-only numeric is per-unit), R64 governs Python/TS unit types and rows stating regime+unit, R72's 'required field on the record' is `console_legacy_usd_statement.rollout_hold boolean`, already in SEAMS and checked by `check_seams`; R65 is untouched. The invariant A1's evidence item 2 actually claims as checked is 'no function reads both units, which D1R's unit scan checks', and its natural single-edit mutant (inline the USD sum in `claim_signup_grant`) is demonstrably killed — evidence drill 2 records the scan firing on exactly that, which is why 38aea7f split the function out. The residual is a known limit of D1R's name-tokenised scan (a USD read behind a non-matching helper name), owned by track D, not an A1 defect; the helper is also `revoke all … from service_role`, so it is not an offered DTO/function surface. A return-type shape assertion would be a hardening nicety, not a gate.

nonblocking.claim_broken: 'Denials recorded' (infrx.signup_denials) does not hold on the G6B operator path: the claim runs inside `conn.transaction()`, and answer() raising Forbidden for identity_reused/rollout_hold/retired rolls back the denial row the function just recorded.
nonblocking.evidence: Probe P5 on both images: PgSignup.grant_initial for a second account on a claimed address raised 'Forbidden: signup grant refused: identity_reused' and signup_denials had 0 rows for that user; the same user through a direct claim_signup_grant answered identity_reused with attempts=1. No money moves either way (the refusal carries no grant), so this is an audit gap, not a ledger defect.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: In grant_initial, when status is a denial, exit the transaction cleanly (commit) before raising - e.g. compute `status` and `row` inside the transaction, call answer() outside it - so the denial row persists; the rollback is only needed for the org-mismatch case after a granted/replayed status.

nonblocking.claim_broken: Retention/lawfulness of the digest: `sha256(lower(btrim(email)))` is unsalted and unkeyed, so it is dictionary-reversible (hash any candidate address list and match) — it is pseudonymised personal data, not anonymised. It is also made immutable by `forbid_update_delete`, so an erasure decision needs a schema change. A per-row salt would defeat its purpose (cross-account matching) and a pepper cannot live in the DB, so the design is defensible for fraud control under legitimate interest; but retention after retirement is an OPEN LEGAL INPUT (the evidence itself lists it under P-05/P-09), not lawful-by-design.
nonblocking.evidence: Static: table definition and trigger at the cited lines; probe P9 (dictionary hit on the fixture addresses) not run. The implementer's own evidence: 'Open for the coordinator/legal ... whether the digest's retention is bounded'.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: Record in 08 §10 (R-A1) that the digest is pseudonymous personal data retained for abuse control with a bounded period decided by legal (P-05), and that erasure requires dropping the immutability trigger for that row; no code change until ruled.
